refNota: Use the attached image as the reference for the person, her clothes and the room. SAME woman: Mexican, 29 years old, warm brown skin, the same face, the same eyebrows, the same features, the same long dark wavy hair worn the same way, the same small gold hoop earrings, the same oversized cream knit sweater, the same black leggings, the same white sneakers. SAME ROOM, element by element: the same spare bedroom of an ordinary Mexican house, the same cream painted wall, the same long galvanized steel pipe clothing rack running left to right across the back wall, the same second shorter pipe rack at frame right, the same window at frame right with the same sheer white curtain and the same soft overcast daylight, the same beige ceramic tile floor with the same grout lines, the same folding table at right foreground. SAME camera: the same eye-level medium-wide 35 mm shot from the same position and the same distance, the same white balance, the same framing, and she stands in the same spot of the frame, in front of the rack, as in the reference.
escena: Same woman, same clothes, same room, same camera and same framing as the attached reference photograph — only the mess and her mood have changed. She now stands relaxed and smiling in the same spot in front of the rack, both hands complete and clearly her own, holding a tablet in both hands with the screen on and angled toward the camera showing a clean list of customer rows, each row with a small round avatar, a colored status dot and a small countdown pill. ELEMENT BY ELEMENT, EVERYTHING STAYS AND ONLY GETS TIDY: the same cream painted wall, now with the pink and yellow sticky notes peeled off, the paint and its uneven patches unchanged; the same long galvanized steel pipe rack across the back wall with the same garments, now evenly spaced on matching wooden hangers and grouped by color with plain colored disc dividers on the pipe, the scraps of paper taped onto the garments gone; the same shorter pipe rack at frame right with the same beige and terracotta trousers, now hanging straight and evenly; the same window at frame right with the same sheer white curtain and the same soft overcast daylight; the same beige ceramic tile floor, now completely clear — the piles of loose garments, the spilled open cardboard boxes and the plastic bags that covered it are gone, the boxes flattened and stacked against the wall; the same folding table at right foreground, now wiped clear with three sealed parcels stacked squarely on it, their blank labels aligned, a small digital shipping scale beside them, the spiral notebook closed and pushed to the far edge, the loose tape rolls and tangled mailers gone, the second phone resting face up on a small stand showing a single tidy chat thread; the same bed against the side wall, now with the folded stacks squared into neat piles. THIS IS STILL THE ROOM OF A HOUSE, NOT A STUDIO AND NOT A SHOP: keep the tile floor, the painted wall, the galvanized pipe, the folding table and the bed visible — there must be no smooth white minimalist wall, no black-framed floor-to-ceiling window, no view of glass towers, no black showroom rail with color separators, no seamless studio backdrop, no polished concrete or wooden showroom floor, no shop counter, no retail signage. No second person, no extra garments brought in, no furniture that was not in the reference. Calm and in control. HANDS AND BODIES: every hand is complete and anatomically correct with five separate well-formed fingers and visible nails, no fused, melted or mitten-like hands; every arm belongs to a person who is visible in the frame, is of natural length and is clearly attached to that person's own shoulder — no floating or orphan hands, no third hand, no extra limbs, no rubbery stretched arms, no impossible elbows; nobody carries something with one arm while at the same time grabbing something else with a hand that cannot be theirs; it is visually obvious who is holding each object; NOTHING FLOATS — every garment is either hooked on a hanger that hangs on the galvanized pipe, on a dress form, folded in a stack, inside a box or inside a bag, never held loose in the air, never suspended by itself, never inflating or ballooning with empty sleeves opening out; every laptop, tablet, phone and box rests on a real surface or is held in two complete visible hands. NO TEXT: no readable text, letters or numbers anywhere in the image — not on garments, boxes, labels, tags, notebooks, parcels, packaging, price cards or signage; no logos, no brand marks, no courier markings, no QR codes, no barcodes; garment prints are plain colors, simple stripes or small flowers, never a garbled or melted graphic; every screen is ON, clearly visible and shows abstract interface only — rows with small round avatars, colored status dots, small countdown pills, garment thumbnails, colored size blocks, soft grey placeholder lines — never words, never numbers, never a grey or switched-off screen, never the back of the device. PRINTED IMAGERY: no printed or displayed image inside the frame — catalogs, posters, packaging, boxes, cards or screens — may show a person in underwear or an uncovered body; everybody in frame is fully and modestly dressed in everyday clothes. Editorial documentary photography, 35 mm, real Mexican people working, natural daylight, photorealistic, shallow depth of field, not a 3D render, not an illustration, not a stock studio setup.
